paper_metadata.title: Myoclonic seizures subside in the fourth decade in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a sample from a tertiary referral center which may introduce selection bias toward more severe cases, though the authors note many primary care admissions. The recruitment process from a historical cohort (1972-1996) into a prospective phase (1997-2006) is well-described, but the final sample of 48 is a small fraction of the original 156 files analyzed, raising concerns about the representativeness of those who remained in long-term follow-up.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: retrospectively analyzed the files of 156 patients diagnosed with JME according to the criteria of International League Against Epilepsy7 between 1972 and 1996 in our epilepsy outpatient clinic.
items.reasoning: The source population and diagnostic criteria are clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This epilepsy center is a part of a university hospital and a well-established tertiary referral center for patients with epilepsy in Turkey. On the other hand... admittance of the patients for primary neurology and emergency departments are also common.
items.reasoning: While the setting is described, the transition from 156 retrospective files to the 51 initially enrolled for prospective follow-up is not fully detailed regarding potential selection bias.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 1972 and 1996... The prospective evaluation began in 1997 and the analyses included all data retrospectively and prospectively collected between 1972 and 2006.
items.reasoning: The timeline for both retrospective identification and prospective follow-up is explicit.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Istanbul University, Istanbul Medical Faculty, Department of Neurology, Millet Cad, 34390, Capa, Istanbul, Turkey
items.reasoning: The specific institution and geographic location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: diagnosed with JME according to the criteria of International League Against Epilepsy7... patients having a minimum follow-up duration of 7 years in our institution were included without any other exclusion criteria
items.reasoning: Criteria include standard diagnostic guidelines and a specific minimum follow-up duration.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not provide the total number of eligible patients from the original 156 who were invited versus those who agreed to the prospective phase, making it impossible to calculate a participation rate.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We enrolled 48 patients (29 F, 19 M; aged 39.9 ± 9.5 years) followed up for a mean of 19.6 ± 5.7 years.
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical characteristics are summarized in the text and Table 1.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for the final cohort of 48 patients with high detail. While there was a high rate of 'delayed visits' (73%), the authors used proactive methods (phone/letters) to maintain follow-up, and the mean follow-up duration is exceptionally long (nearly 20 years).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: The remaining 48 patients were reevaluated in 2006.
items.reasoning: Of the 51 initially enrolled for the prospective phase, 48 (94%) were included in the final analysis (3 were excluded for diagnostic revisions, not loss to follow-up).

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: If the patients delayed the scheduled visits for more than 1 year, they were invited to a subsequent visit with telephone calls or letters.
items.reasoning: The authors describe active measures to minimize attrition.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 2 patients with progressive course who were diagnosed with Lafora disease... and one last patient having partial epilepsy... were excluded from follow-up.
items.reasoning: Reasons for exclusion from the prospective cohort are clearly stated.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up

items.reasoning: There is no description of the characteristics of the ~100 patients from the original retrospective pool who did not make it into the prospective cohort.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No comparison is provided between the analyzed cohort and those lost between the retrospective and prospective phases.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (age, clinical features, EEG) were measured using standard clinical protocols by experienced epileptologists. The use of independent evaluation by two experts reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The clinical and EEG features, antiepileptic drug (AED) treatment regimen, and systemic and psychiatric comorbid diseases were evaluated.
items.reasoning: The factors being studied as predictors of outcome are clearly listed.

items.evidence_snippet: All patients were independently evaluated by at least two of the experienced epileptologists during the longterm follow-up.
items.reasoning: Independent evaluation by multiple experts is a strong indicator of reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

items.evidence_snippet: No specific treatment regimen, laboratory investigations, or EEG controls were planned for them and they were managed according to clinical needs, like all other patients with IGE.
items.reasoning: Standardized clinical care in a single center ensures consistency in measurement setting.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary outcome (seizure remission/severity) relies heavily on patient self-reporting and retrospective recall for the early years of the study. While the prospective phase mitigates this, the 'alleviation' metric is subjective.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Remission was defined as ever being seizure-free for an individual seizure type... at least for 5 years... The patient's self-assessment was used basically to rate the myoclonus severity: 0: no myoclonus; 1: milder; 2: same severity
items.reasoning: Definitions for remission and severity changes are explicitly provided.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The patient's self-assessment was used basically to rate the myoclonus severity
items.reasoning: Self-assessment of seizure frequency and severity is standard but prone to recall bias, especially over a 20-year period.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The changes in severity/frequency of myoclonia were systematically questioned.
items.reasoning: A systematic questioning approach was applied to the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies and measures several important confounders (AED types, psychiatric comorbidities, thyroid disease). However, the analysis relies on univariable comparisons (Fisher exact tests) rather than multivariable modeling, which limits the ability to control for multiple confounders simultaneously.

items.reasoning: Treatment and psychiatric categories are defined, but 'lifestyle problems' are somewhat vaguely described.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the descriptive and exploratory nature of the study. The use of Kaplan-Meier curves for myoclonus freedom is a strength. Reporting is transparent regarding the small sample size limitations.
